text: Ryder was just under three. Just under three. I mean, I was kind of begging, begging for a diagnosis so that I could get him diagnosed I mean, I knew, having three children before he was born, you know, I knew that he wasn't meeting certain milestones. I mean, specifically language, you know? And a doctor kept telling me to wait. Every child is different, you know? I'm like, I feel like he should be talking. I finally just begged enough so that he gave me a written diagnosis. But see, I live in California and we have like legislation that is specific to special needs and dis- In order for me to take advantage of early intervention things at the regional center, which is where we go to get our supports and services, I needed a written diagnosis. I think it was more fear, but I mean, with the help of other parents, thank God, who helped me early. It was another parent who became my first advocate. And then I wanted to do the same thing as I've grown and I'm still learning and still navigating this walk, but I've learned so much. I met a parent there like who told me, no, you got to go beg, you got to beg for it. Go to the regional center, go here, do this. I'll come with you. You know, just that type of stuff. Knowing that there is someone else who knows a little bit more than I know and who's sort of walking the same walk, you know? And that was really why I did. It started my foundation writers room just to be able to not gatekeep, you know, and share what I'm learning. And then we can learn together, we can cry together, vent together, you know what I mean? I love that. I love it.
